BILL NUMBER: S4777

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general construction law, the banking law, the
correction law, the civil practice law and rules, the debtor and credi-
tor law, the domestic relations law, the mental hygiene law, the real
property actions and proceedings law, the New York City civil court act,
the uniform city court act, the uniform district court act, and the
uniform justice court act, in relation to replacing certain instances of
the word "mentally ill person" with "person with a mental disability";
and to repeal certain provisions of the general construction law relat-
ing thereto

 
PURPOSE:

To replace outdated and insensitive language found in Section 28 of the
general construction law as it relates to language describing or defin-
ing (a) mental disability.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 replaces the definition of mental disability in Section 28 of
the general construction law, using instead the definition offered in
section 1.03 of mental hygiene law.

Section 2 amends section 100 of the banking law, replacing "mentally
ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 3 amends section 100-a of the banking law, replacing "mentally
ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 4 amends Section 402 of the correction law, replacing "mentally
ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 5 amends Subparagraph (i) of paragraph b of subdivision 2 of
section 508 of the correction law, replacing "mentally ill" and adding
"with a mental disability."

Section 6 amends Section 4519 of the civil practice law and rules,
replacing "mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 7 amends Section 251 of the debtor and creditor law, replacing
"mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 8 amends Subdivisions ( c) and (f) of section 140 of the domes-
tic relations law, replacing "mentally ill and adding "with a mental
disability."

Section 9 amends Section 141 of the domestic relations law, "mentally
ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 10 amends Section 142 of the domestic relations law, replacing
"mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 11 amends the article heading of article 9 of the mental hygiene
law, replacing "mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 12 amends Section 9.03 of the mental hygiene law, replacing
"mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 13 amends Section 9.35 of the mental hygiene law, replacing
"mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 14 amends the section heading of section 9.47 of the mental
hygiene law, replacing "mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disabil-
ity."

Section 15 amends subdivision (a) of section 9.47 of the mental hygiene
law, replacing "mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 16 amends the opening paragraph of section 9.47 of the mental
hygiene law, replacing "mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disabil-
ity."

Section 17 amends subparagraph (iii) of paragraph 1 of subdivision (b)
of section 31.16 of the mental hygiene law, replacing "mentally ill" and
adding "with a mental disability."

Section 18 amends Subdivision 1 of section 1531 of the real property
actions and proceedings law, replacing "mentally ill" and adding "with a
mental disability."

Section 19 amends subdivisions 1, 3 and 4 of section 1651 of the real
property actions and proceedings law, replacing "mentally ill" and
adding "with a mental disability."

Section 20 Section 1804 of the New York city civil court act, replacing
"mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 21 Amends Section 1804-A of the New York city civil court act,
replacing "mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 22 amends Section 1804 of the uniform city court act, replacing
"mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 23 amends 1804-A of the uniform city court act, replacing
"mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 24 amends Section 1804 of the uniform district court act,
replacing "mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 25 amends Section 1804-A of the uniform district court act, as
added by chapter 653 of the laws of 1987, replacing "mentally ill" and
adding "with a mental disability."

Section 26 amends Section 1804 of the uniform justice court act, replac-
ing "mentally ill" and adding "with a mental disability."

Section 27 Effective Date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The aim of this bill is to remove outdated and insensitive language from
the law as it relates to any person living with a mental disability, so
as to reflect the progress made in realizing and ensuring the civil
rights of individuals living with a mental health disorder, intellectual
or developmental disabilities (I/DD), or addictive disorder. The defi-
nition as it exists from Section 28 from the General Construction Law
will be replaced by existing language used in the Mental Hygiene Law
1.03, thereby creating consistency between the two sections of law and
removing any descriptive suggestion that they are any less than any
other person under the letter of the law.

The removal of Section 28 from the General Construction Law will repre-
sent progress both in the spirit of our laws, as well as progress in the
literal letter of the law. Currently, Section 28 from the General
Construction Law describes a person with a mental disability as follows
"The terms lunatic, mentally ill person, lunacy and mental illness
include every kind of unsoundness of mind except idiocy or mental retar-
dation."

The language as it exists suggests that individuals with a mental disa-
bility are less-than, made plainly clear by the use of the word lunat-
ic'. Therefore, it is imperative that the language be removed and
replaced by existing language used in the Mental Hygiene Law 1.03.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately
